BURSEVI:v1p345/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r1.claim: Invalidating charity means losing its reward, not undoing the completed act; boasting and harm earn no reward and incur wrong against the recipient.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r1.anchor: والمراد بإبطال الصدقة إحباط أجرها لأن الصدقة لما وقعت وتقدمت لم يمكن أن يراد بإبطالها نفسها

BURSEVI:v1p345/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r2.claim: The comparison is to a hypocrite who spends to be seen and praised, without belief or hope for God's approval and the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r2.anchor: المراد المنافق لأن الكافر معلن كفره غير مراء والكاف في محل النصب على أنه صفة لمصدر محذوف

BURSEVI:v1p345/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r3.claim: Riyāʾ is a reciprocal form because the giver acts while attending to the people's seeing and praise.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r3.anchor: ومعنى المفاعلة ههنا مبني على أن المرائي في الإنفاق يراعي أن تراه الناس فيحمدوه

BURSEVI:v1p345/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r4.claim: Ṣafwān is a smooth stone with a little dust; a heavy downpour strips it bare so no covering remains.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r4.anchor: حجر صاف أملس وهو واحد وجمع فمن جعله جمعا فواحده صفوانة

BURSEVI:v1p345/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r5.claim: The dissemblers cannot benefit from what they earned or receive any reward, like deeds made scattered dust in the cited verse.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r5.anchor: لا ينتفعون بما فعلوا رئاء ولا يجدون له ثوابا قطعا كقوله تعالى : {فجعلناه هباء منثورا}

BURSEVI:v1p345/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r6.claim: The plural pronoun refers to the generic individual or group represented by الذي; the singular relative can also convey the sense of من.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r6.anchor: أراد بالذي ينفق الجنس أو الفريق الذي ينفق ولأن من والذي يتعاقبان

BURSEVI:v1p345/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r7.claim: The parable first makes the clearest case—a disbeliever's worthless spending—then compares its stripping away to the loss of charity's reward through boasting and harm.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r7.anchor: فمثله أولا بمن ينفق ماله رئاء الناس وهو مع ذلك كافر بالله واليوم الآخر

BURSEVI:v1p345/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345/r8.claim: The Muʿtazilite account treats good works as establishing reward that major sins can erase; the author's Ashʿarite colleagues say no reward had been established because the gift was never sincerely devotional.
BURSEVI:v1p345/r8.anchor: وذلك صريح في القول بالإحباط والتكفير كما ذهب إليه المعتزلة القائلون بأن الأعمال الصالحة توجب الثواب

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r1.claim: The author favors the Ashʿarite reading: reward is a pure divine gift, and boasting makes the gift a donation to the recipient rather than a sincere deed offered to God for promised reward.
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r1.anchor: فقد جرى على سنن المبادلة التي وقعت

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r2.claim: Since good deeds are treated as a loan or transaction with God, a donor should not boast to the poor; boasting turns away from God and means the deed was empty from the start.
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r2.anchor: فلما كانت معاملته في الحقيقة مع الله تعالى لم يبق وجه

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r3.claim: The warning about God not guiding disbelievers implies that ostentation, boasting, and injury are traits believers must avoid.
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r3.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن كلا من الرئاء والمن والأذى من خصائص الكفار ولا بد للمؤمنين أن يجتنبوها

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r4.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r4.claim: An unnamed scholar compares ostentatious worship to carrying a sack of stones: observers may praise its fullness, but it buys nothing.
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r4.anchor: روي عن بعض العلماء أنه قال مثل من يعمل الطاعة للرئاء والسمعة كمثل رجل خرج إلى السوق

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r5.claim: Early donors hid charity in several ways: seeking blind recipients, attaching money to a sleeping poor person's clothing, or leaving it where a poor person would find it.
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r5.anchor: وقد بالغ السلف في إخفاء صدقتهم عن أعين الناس حتى طلب بعضهم فقيرا أعمى

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r6.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r6.claim: Rumi's poem urges worshippers to seek God's guidance and ask that prayer not be mixed with the prayer of the misguided or ostentatious.

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r7.claim: The Prophet calls ostentation the minor shirk he fears for the community and says God will tell those who sought human notice to seek their reward from those people.
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r7.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : "إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم الشرك الأصغر"

BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r8.claim: A hadith says a Qur'an reciter, a martyr, and a wealthy donor are first brought to judgment; each is condemned for seeking fame rather than God's approval and becomes fuel for Hell.
BURSEVI:v1p345#2/r8.anchor: أول من يدعى به رجل جمع القرآن ورجل قتل في سبيل الله ورجل كثير المال

BURSEVI:v1p346/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r1.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p346/r1.claim: Saʿdī's Persian verses urge humility, hiding spiritual emptiness, and resisting the wish for public fame or praise.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r1.anchor: طريقت همينست كاهل يقين نكو كار بودند وتقصير بين

BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.claim: In the inward reading, transactions mixed with ulterior aims turn away from God and toward falsehood, thereby invalidating acts of devotion; after truth there is only error.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r2.anchor: والإشارة في الآية في المعاملات إذا كانت مشوبة بالأغراض ففيها نوع من الأعراض

BURSEVI:v1p346/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346/r3.claim: Reminding a poor person of charity shows the giver sought the recipient rather than God; if the goal were God, the giver would feel indebted to the poor person as a means of reaching Him.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r3.anchor: إذا مننت بها على الفقير فقد أعرضت عن طلب الحق لأن قصدك في الصدقة لو كان طلب الحق

BURSEVI:v1p346/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p346/r4.claim: The hadith that the rich would perish without the poor is interpreted to mean that poor recipients give the rich a way to reach God.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r4.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "لولا الفقراء لهلك الأغنياء" معناه لم يجدوا وسيلة إلى الحق

BURSEVI:v1p346/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346/r5.claim: One interpretation reverses 'the upper hand is better': the poor person has the upper hand and the rich donor the lower, since the donor gives and receives through the poor.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r5.anchor: وقد فسر بعضهم قوله عليه السلام : "اليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى" بأن اليد العليا هي يد الفقير

BURSEVI:v1p346/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346/r6.claim: In the inward reading, harm means turning toward anything other than the Real, which corrupts acts when they are mixed with worldly or otherworldly motives.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r6.anchor: والأذى هو الإقبال على الباطل لأن كل شيء غير الحق فهو باطل

BURSEVI:v1p346/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r7.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
BURSEVI:v1p346/r7.claim: Rumi's poetry says the lover's joy and grief, service, and wage belong to the beloved; love for any other gain is a futile fantasy.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r7.anchor: عاشقا نرا شادماني وغم اوست دست مزد واجرت خدمت هم اوست

BURSEVI:v1p346/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346/r8.claim: When divine love dominates the heart, it severs attachment to wealth, children, and one's own life as rival claims.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r8.anchor: فالعشق الإلهي والحب الرحماني إذا استولى على قلب العبد يقطع عنه عرق الشركة

BURSEVI:v1p346/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346/r9.claim: A spiritually mature servant does not serve for wages; trusting the master's generosity frees the heart from watching for payment.
BURSEVI:v1p346/r9.anchor: والخدمة بالأجرة لا تناسب الرجولية فإن من علم أن مولاه كريم يقطع قلبه عن ملاحظة الأجرة

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r10.claim: The continuation cites a Hafiz couplet advising the servant to trust the master's generosity instead of demanding wages.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r10.anchor: تو بندكى وكدايان بشرط مزد مكن

BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r11.claim: The closing prayer asks God to sever hope from everything else and make the worshippers seek only His essence.
BURSEVI:v1p346#2/r11.anchor: اللهم اقطع رجاءنا عن غيرك واجعلنا من الذين لا يطلبون منك إلا ذاتك

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p136/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p136/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والزهري
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p136/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhrī read صفوان with fatḥa on fāʾ; the pattern فعْلان is common in descriptions and verbal nouns but possible in other nouns too.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p136/r4.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة سعيد بن المسيب والزهري: "كمثل صفوان عليه تراب"

QIRAAT-ER:2:264:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:264:16#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:264:16#1/r1.claim: The hamza is resolved to yāʾ, smoothing the pronunciation without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:2:264:16#1/r1.anchor: Hamza resolution: riʾāʾ → riyāʾ; the hamza is replaced by yāʾ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#2/r1.claim: Qatada glosses ṣald as bare and clean, with nothing left on it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p107#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ فتركه صلدا ﴾ قال نقيا ليس عليه شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r2.claim: رئاء is a verbal noun of showing people one’s good deed so they praise and honor the giver, with no other intention.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r2.anchor: الرئاء: فعال مصدر من راء من الرؤية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r3.claim: The source defines صفوان as a large smooth stone and records disagreements: some use it as a collective, al-Kisāʾī gives singular/plural analyses, and al-Mubarrad rejects his proposals; Abū Ḥayyān also rejects al-Kisāʾī’s account.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r3.anchor: الصفوان: الحجر الكبير الأملس، وتحريك فائه بالفتح لغة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r4.claim: تراب also appears as توراب; ترب means becoming poor while أترب means becoming rich, the hamza removing dust/poverty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r4.anchor: التراب: معروف ويقال فيه توراب، وترب الرجل افتقر، واترب استغنى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r5.speaker: النضر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r5.claim: Al-Naḍr lists rainfall stages from light رش and طس through drizzle and drops to heavy rain and generous downpour.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r5.anchor: وقال النضر: أول ما يكون المطر رشا، ثم طسا، ثم طلا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r6.claim: صلد is bare, smooth stone stripped of its dust; other authorities call it a bare surface, a soft stone, or anything devoid of good, and the source notes related usage for slow-boiling pots.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p650/r6.anchor: الصلد: الأجرد الأملس النقي من التراب الذي كان عليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r4.claim: The prohibition repeats because the conditions already stated were not enough: reproach and injury invalidate charity, and the believers’ identity is invoked to strengthen avoidance; invalidation means no reward with God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r4.anchor: لم يكتف بذلك حتى جعل المن والأذى مبطلا للصدقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r5.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r5.claim: Al-Suddī believes sins do not cancel good deeds; the majority instead say God does not accept charity from someone known to reproach and injure recipients, while another view says the angel is marked not to record it because its intention is not God’s.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r5.anchor: والسدي يعتقد أن السيئات لا تبطل الحسنات، فقال جمهور العلماء:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r6.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r6.claim: Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār argues that the charity already occurred and cannot be undone, so the verse means that later reproach cancels its future reward; Abū Ḥayyān says both readings fit, while the verse repeats warnings to stress the wrong and singles out charity because reproach is especially ugly there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r6.anchor: وقال القاضي عبد الجبار: معلوم أن الصدقة قد وقعت وتقدمت،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r7.claim: The apparent meaning makes المن injury directed toward the poor recipient, which is the majority view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p661/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: بالمن، معناه على الفقير، وهو قول الجمهور.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says reproach is directed toward God because of the charity, while injury is directed toward the petitioner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: بالمن على الله تعالى بسبب صدقته، والأذى للسائل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r2.claim: The كاف may modify an omitted verbal noun, “invalidating like the invalidation by the one who spends for show,” or describe the addressees’ state as resembling such a spender.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r2.anchor: و: الكاف، قيل في موضع نعت لمصدر محذوف تقديره إبطالا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r3.claim: Zamakhsharī takes the spender as a hypocrite who gives for reputation and praise, not God or the afterlife, which he inwardly disbelieves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r3.anchor: وفي هذا المنافق قولان: أحدهما: أنه المنافق، ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r4.speaker: مفسرون غير مسمين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies him as an openly unbelieving person who gives only to win public praise; Makkī prefers the hypocrite because ostentation fits someone concealing disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r4.anchor: وقيل: المراد به الكافر المجاهر، وذلك بإنفاقه لقول الناس: ما أكرمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r5.claim: رئاء is parsed either as a purpose complement or as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r5.anchor: وانتصاب رئاء على أنه مفعول من أجله، أو مصدر في موضع الحال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r6.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r6.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif reads رياء, replacing the first hamza with yāʾ because of the preceding kasra; this reading is also reported from ʿĀṣim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف: رياء بإبدال الهمزة الأولى ياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r7.claim: The pronoun in فمثله most naturally returns to the nearest antecedent, the ostentatious spender, whether hypocrite or openly boastful unbeliever; another view makes it the reproachful giver and understands two successive comparisons.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r7.anchor: فالظاهر أنه عائد على كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس لقربه منه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r8.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r8.claim: ʿAbd al-Jabbār says the verse first compares reproachful charity to a showy unbeliever and then to dust washed from a bare stone, proving reproach cancels reward after it accrued; Abū Ḥayyān notes this depends on his earlier theory and that the analogy can instead show an initially invalid gift.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p662/r8.anchor: قال القاضي عبد الجبار: ذكر تعالى لكيفية إبطال الصدقة بالمن والأذى مثلين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r1.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار وأصحابه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilite reading treats the rain as reproach and injury removing reward after it was earned; others take the dust as charity already paired with corrupt intent, only apparently attached to the stone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r1.anchor: وأما التمثيل الثاني فإنه عند عبد الجيار وأصحابه، جعل الوابل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r2.claim: The second interpretation is stronger because dust rests visibly on stone without adhering or sinking in; likewise, giving with reproach appears charitable but is not truly so, so the verse can mean preventing either reward or charity from the outset.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r2.anchor: قيل: والحمل عى هذا المعنى أولى، لأن التراب إذا وقع على الصفوان لم يكن ملتصقا به،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r3.speaker: ابن المسيب، والزهري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r3.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhrī read صفوان with fatḥa on fāʾ; the source calls this irregular in ordinary usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن المسيب، والزهري: صفوان بفتح الفاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r4.claim: تراب is the subject of an understood “settled upon”; فأصابه coordinates with that verb, its pronoun may refer to the stone or dust, while فتركه refers to the stone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r4.anchor: وارتفع تراب على الفاعلية، أي: استقر عليه تراب، فأصابه وابل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r5.claim: In the image, visible work is dust, the reproachful or hypocritical giver is the stone, and Judgment Day is the rain; on the Muʿtazilite reading, reproach itself is the rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r5.anchor: وهذه الجملة جعل فيها العمل الظاهر: كالتراب، والمان المؤذي، أو المنافق كالصفوان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r6.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r6.claim: Al-Qaffāl offers a seed-store reading: sincere deeds are seed planted in fertile ground and multiplied, while hypocrites sow on bare stone, leaving no crop to retrieve when needed; the analogy therefore implies seed and harvest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p663/r6.anchor: وقال القفال: وفيه احتمال آخر، وهو أن أعمال العباد ذخائر لهم يوم القيامة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r1.claim: The plural يقدرون may shift from the addressed believers to a plural sense of the generic كالذي; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says switching back after following the singular form is contrary to the usual Arabic pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r1.anchor: اختلف في الضمير في: يقدرون، فقيل:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r2.speaker: مفسرون غير مسمين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r2.claim: Another view supplies a generic referent: no one can use the seed in dust washed from the bare stone; likewise the reproachful donor, hypocrite, or unbeliever cannot benefit from deeds at Judgment, their intended earnings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو عائد على معلوم غير مذكور المعنى لا يقدر أحد من الخلق على الانتفاع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r3.claim: Calling expenditure كسب reflects the donors’ aim to earn; related verses portray deeds performed without God’s approval as scattered dust, windblown ash, or a mirage, and a report describes the first judged as a martyr, scholar, and donor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r3.anchor: وعبروا عن النفقة بالكسب لأنهم قصدوا بها الكسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r4.claim: Allah’s عدم guidance means He does not guide people persisting in unbelief either out of their disbelief or in their deeds while they remain unbelievers; this favors the interpretation that the parable depicts a disbeliever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p664/r4.anchor: وفي هذا ترجح لمن قال: إن ضرب المثل عائد على الكافر.

SULAMI:v1p79#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p79#3/r1.speaker: السري
SULAMI:v1p79#3/r1.claim: Whoever adorns himself with his deeds turns good deeds into sins; how much worse is one who claims their value and seeks compensation for them?
SULAMI:v1p79#3/r1.anchor: قال السري : من تزين بعمله كانت حسناته سيئات ، فكيف من رأى له قيمة وطلب عليه العوض ؟

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.claim: The direct address to believers follows third-person description to strengthen the command; the charity is spoiled by either reproach or injury, with reproach usually directed to the poor.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.anchor: أقبل عليهم بالخطاب إثر بيان ما بين بطريق الغيبة البالغة في إيجاب العمل بموجب النهي

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to interpret reproach as being directed toward God; injury is directed toward the poor recipient.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.anchor: المراد به المن على الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that the verse appears to say either reproach or injury cancels charity, although the gift has occurred and Sunni doctrine says sins do not cancel good deeds, unlike the Muʿtazilite position.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.anchor: وإستشكل ابن عطية هذه الآية بأن ظاهرها يستدعي أن أجر الصدقة يبطل بأحد هذين الأمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.claim: The answer offered is that God never accepts a gift from someone He knows will reproach or hurt its recipient; some say an angel is marked not to record it, so no accepted deed is later annulled.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.anchor: وأجيب بأن الصدقة التي يعلم الله تعالى من صاحبها أنه يمن ويؤذي لا تقبل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.claim: That answer means do not perform the act as an invalid gift, rather than canceling a valid accepted deed; the author admits this departs from the apparent wording, though the simile partly supports it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.anchor: حينئذ لا تأتوا بهذا العمل باطلا كذا قالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.claim: The phrase comparing the donor to one who spends for show may modify an implied noun for nullifying or describe the acting donors’ state; the latter supports the proposed answer because ostentation is never accepted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.anchor: في محل نصب إما على أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف أي لا تبطلوها إبطالا كإبطال الذي الخ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.claim: Riyāʾ can be the purpose of spending or the donor’s state; its verbal form is reciprocal because the donor displays deeds and people return praise and honor.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.anchor: إما على أنه علة لينفق أي لأجل ريائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r8.speaker: الخزاعي، الشموني
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r8.claim: Al-Khuzāʿī and al-Shamūnī are among those who read the first hamza of riyāʾ lightly as a yāʾ to avoid the weight of a hamza after kasra.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r8.anchor: ويجوز تخفيف الهمزة الأولى بأن تقلب ياءا فرارا من ثقل الهمزة بعد الكسرة وقد قرأ به الخزاعي والشموني

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r9.claim: Some say the ostentatious donor may be a believer or unbeliever, but most commentators take him as a hypocrite because he does not believe in God and the Last Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r9.anchor: والمراد من الموصول ما يشمل المؤمن والكافر كما قيل وغالب المفسرين على أن المراد به المنافق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r10.claim: Ṣafwān is a large smooth stone, whether analyzed as a collective, a plural, or a genus noun; its thin dust is washed away by a powerful downpour.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r10.anchor: أي حجر كبير أملس وهو جمع صفوانة أو صفاء أو إسم جنس

ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r11.claim: The comparison can map stone, dust, and rain separately to the useless donor, apparent hope of reward, and ostentation, or work as one composite image; a reported view calls the composite the right reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p34#3/r11.anchor: وهذا التشبيه يجوز أن يكون مفرقا فالنافق المنافق كالحجر في عدم الإنتفاع

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r1.claim: The ostentatious donor can attain no reward or benefit from what he spent; this either explains the comparison or answers an implied question about its outcome.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r1.anchor: أي لا يجدون ثواب شيء مما أنفقوا رياءا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r2.speaker: السمين
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r2.claim: Al-Samīn’s suggestion that the clause is a circumstantial modifier of the relative antecedent is judged weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r2.anchor: وجعلها حال من الذي كما قال : السمين مهزول من القول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r3.claim: The plural pronoun may refer to the singular-form relative by meaning; alternatives include collective usage or treating man and alladhī as interchangeable, while return to the believers is dismissed.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r3.anchor: والضمير راجع إلى الموصول بإعتبار المعنى بعدما روعي لفظه إذ هو صفة لمفرد لفظا مجموع معنى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r4.claim: God’s statement that He does not guide the unbelieving people closes the argument and implies reproach, injury, and ostentation are traits believers must avoid.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p35/r4.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن كلا من الرياء والمن والأذى على الإنفاق من صفات الكفار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says charity is nullified by reminding God of one's gift, as well as by hurting the recipient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: بالمن على الله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r6.claim: The show-off's gift resembles soil washed from a smooth stone: apparent deeds vanish on the Day of Judgment because they were not for God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r6.anchor: فإذا كان يوم القيامة بطل كله واضمحل لأنه لم يكن لله عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r7.claim: This comparison includes the hypocrite, the show-off, and the believer who reminds and hurts; they seem to have deeds as the stone seems to hold soil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r7.anchor: فهذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى لنفقة المنافق والمرائي والمؤمن الذي يمن بصدقته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r8.claim: The disbelievers cannot obtain reward for what they earned, and God does not guide disbelieving people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r8.anchor: {لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا} أي على ثواب شيء مما كسبوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r9.speaker: محمود بن لبيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r9.claim: Mahmud ibn Labid reports that the Prophet feared lesser shirk for his community and identified it as showing off; at judgment, God will direct show-offs to seek reward from those they performed for.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p326/r9.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال "إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم الشرك الأصغر"

NAHHAS:v1p333/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p333/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p333/r3.claim: Arab idiom distinguishes gifts followed by reminders, unsolicited giving, and requested giving; Abu Ja'far prefers singular صفوان.
NAHHAS:v1p333/r3.anchor: العرب تقول لما يمن به يد سوداء ولما يعطى عن غير مسألة يد بيضاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r1.claim: Reproach and harm cancel the reward of charity, as does the hypocrite's public show of giving without seeking God's pleasure or the afterlife.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r1.anchor: لا تحبطوا أجرها بكل واحد منهما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r2.claim: The comparison may make the donors like the show-off, or make their charity like his; the syntax allows a source or circumstantial comparison, and riya may mark purpose, state, or manner.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r2.anchor: { كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر } كإبطال المنافق الذي يرائي بإنفاقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r3.claim: A smooth stone carries dust that a heavy rain strips away, leaving it bare; the image depicts spending that produces no benefit or reward.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r3.anchor: { كمثل صفوان } كمثل حجر أملس. { عليه تراب فأصابه وابل }

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r4.claim: The plural pronoun can refer to the generic donor by meaning or by number; a cited line likewise shifts from singular alladhi to plural hum.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264/r4.anchor: { لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا } لا ينتفعون بما فعلوا رئاء ولا يجدون له ثوابا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.claim: Believers must avoid ostentation, reproach, and harm, which are here insinuated to be qualities of disbelievers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.anchor: بأن الرئاء والمن والأذى على الإنفاق من صفات الكفار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r1.claim: Mann and harm can match or exceed the charity's reward, effectively nullifying it; the text links this to the inner sincerity of the deed being overtaken by the flaw of ostentation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r1.anchor: فربما وازى عقابهما ثواب الصدقة أو زاد فكان كالإبطال لأوله إلى أن لا ثواب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r2.claim: Ostentation is an act intended to be seen by people, performed heedless of and blind to God's seeing.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r2.anchor: هو الفعل المقصود به رؤية الخلق غفلة عن رؤية الحق وعماية عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r3.claim: The text compares those who boast of or injure recipients with the ostentatious giver, and portrays the latter in his worst state: lacking belief in God and the Last Day.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r3.anchor: ولما شبه المان والمؤذي بالمرائي لأنه أسقط الناس وأدناهم همة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r4.claim: The stone metaphor explains a donation made for show: smooth, hard rock cannot support plant growth, though a thin layer of soil may initially deceive an inexperienced observer.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r4.anchor: وهو صيغة مبالغة من الصفا وهي الحجارة الملس الصلبة التي لا تقبل انصداعها بالنبات

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r5.claim: A downpour strips the shallow soil from the rock and leaves it bare, depicting how ostentation abruptly removes a donation's apparent fruit, unlike a garden whose fertility is an enduring quality.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r5.anchor: أي مطر كثير فأزال التراب عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r6.claim: The wording that the spenders can do nothing with what they earned uses ellipsis by correspondence and says that neither the represented giver nor the example's planter retains any gain.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r6.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك ولما كان الزارع على مثل هذا عجبا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r7.claim: God does not guide those who corrupt their good deeds by harm and ostentation; identifying them as unbelievers is a particularly severe warning to givers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p517/r7.anchor: معلما أنه يعمي البصراء عن أبين الأمور إذا أراد ومهما شاء فعل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.claim: The text presents the unconditioned warning before the positive incentive because preventing harm takes priority over seeking benefit, then returns to warn against boasting and ostentation with a clearer image.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p519/r2.anchor: وقدم مثل العاري عن الشرط عليه لأن درء المفاسد أولى من جلب المصالح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p520/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p520/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p520/r5.claim: Someone who spoils charitable deeds through abuse faces a loss like the orchard owner and his family when their hopes are destroyed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p520/r5.anchor: فحال من رأى في أعماله أو آذى في صدقة ماله في يوم القيامة وأهواله

DURR-FULL:v2p43/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r8.claim: Reproaching or harming a recipient nullifies charity's reward as heavy rain strips soil from a smooth stone.
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك في الآية قال: من أنفق نفقة ثم من بها أو آذى الذي أعطاه النفقة

DURR-FULL:v2p43/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r9.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r9.claim: God warns believers that reproach and harm invalidate charity just as ostentation invalidates it; rain removes the soil from bare rock.
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r9.anchor: عن السدي في الآية قال الله للمؤمنين لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى فتبطل كما بطلت صدقة الرياء

DURR-FULL:v2p43/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي زكريا
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r10.claim: He heard that showing off in one deed can cancel what preceded it.
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r10.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي زكريا قال: بلغني أن الرجل إذا راءى بشيء من عمله

DURR-FULL:v2p43/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r11.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r11.claim: The Prophet lists reproacher of gifts, one who mistreats parents, habitual drinker, believer in magic, and soothsayer among those barred from Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v2p43/r11.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يدخل الجنة منان ولا عاق

DURR-FULL:v2p44/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r1.claim: The Prophet says God will not look at a parent-abuser, habitual drinker, or one who reproaches recipients; three named types also will not enter Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ثلاثة لا ينظر الله إليهم يوم القيامة العاق لوالديه ومدمن الخمر والمنان بما أعطى

DURR-FULL:v2p44/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas was troubled by the warning that a reproacher cannot enter Paradise until he found this verse addressing reproach.
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لا يدخل الجنة منان فشق ذلك علي حتى وجدت في كتاب الله

DURR-FULL:v2p44/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r3.speaker: عمرو بن حريث
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r3.claim: A fighter may return with no credit if hardship leads him to curse his commander and vow never to fight with him again; this is like charity followed by reproach.
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن حريث قال: إن الرجل يغزو ولا يسرق ولا يزني ولا يغل لا يرجع بالكفاف

DURR-FULL:v2p44/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p44/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {صفوان} يقول: الحجر

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r1.claim: Saldan means left with nothing on it; a related gloss says the slab is left clean, like a hypocrite whose gains avail nothing at resurrection.

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r3.claim: Wabil is heavy rain; the parable depicts disbelievers' deeds at resurrection, stripped away as rain leaves a stone bare.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قال: الوابل المطر الشديد وهذا مثل ضربه الله لأعمال الكفار

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r4.claim: Saldan means dry and barren, producing nothing.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فتركه صلدا} قال: يابسا خاسئا لا ينبت شيئا

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r5.claim: In a lexical exchange, Ibn Abbas defines safwan as smooth stone and cites Aws ibn Hajar's poetry as evidence for the word.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع ابن الأزرق سأله عن قوله {صفوان} قال: الحجر الأملس قال: وهل تعرف العرب ذلك

DURR-FULL:v2p45/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas defines saldan as smooth and cites Abu Talib's poetry as evidence for the word.
DURR-FULL:v2p45/r6.anchor: قال: فأخبرني عن قوله {صلدا} قال: أملس قال: وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال: نعم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts a warning that habitual wine drinkers, those who disobey parents, and boastful donors will not enter Paradise; he found this verse addressing the donor and was relieved that sinners could still repent.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : لا يدخل الجنة مدمن خمر ولا عاق ، ولا منان

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says donations are invalidated by reminders and harm just as an ostentatious donation is invalidated.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r2.anchor: عن السدى قوله : لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والاذى فتبطل كما بطلت صدقة الرياء .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r3.claim: Qatada says God disliked this behavior for believers.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم قال . كره الله ذلك للمؤمنين

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r4.claim: Muqatil explains “reminding” as the donor reminding the recipient of the donation.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قول الله تعالى : لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والاذى هو الرجل يمن صدقته

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r5.claim: Muqatil explains “harm” as hurting the person who receives the charity.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r5.anchor: وبه عن مقاتل بن حيان في قول الله : بالمن والاذى قال : يؤذى الذي يتصدق عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r6.claim: Al-Suddi compares ostentatious spending to rain washing soil off a smooth stone: the money is lost to showing off and yields no reward.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r6.anchor: عن السدى ، قوله : كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ، فكذلك هذا الذي ينفق ماله رياء الناس

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r7.claim: Muqatil interprets the one who does not believe in God and the Last Day as a hypocrite.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r7.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قول الله : ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الاخر يعني : المنافق .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains not believing in God as failing to affirm God's oneness.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : ولا يؤمن بالله يعني : لا يصدقون بتوحيد الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r9.claim: Qatada says the smooth-stone parable represents the deeds of unbelievers on Resurrection Day.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p517/r9.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : فمثله كمثل صفوان عليه تراب قال : هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى ، لاعمال الكفار

IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “safwan” as a smooth rock; Ikrima, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, al-Rabi, Qatada, and Muqatil are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : صفوان يعني : الحجر

IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r2.claim: Ikrima explains “wabil” as rain that takes away the soil; al-Rabi and Qatada specify that it is heavy rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ، في قوله : فاصابه وابل والوابل : المطر فذهب بما عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “left bare” as left dry, fruitless, and disgraced.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : فتركه صلدا يقول : فتركه يابسا خاسئا لا ينبت شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r4.claim: Muqatil says those who spend ostentatiously cannot benefit from what they earned: they receive no reward and it will not help them on Judgment Day; the text also notes his explanations came from Successors including al-Dahhak and Jabir ibn Zayd.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قوله الله لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا يعني به : نفقاتهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r5.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r5.claim: Al-Rabi says that on that Day the ostentatious donors can do nothing with their deeds, just as rain leaves the stone clean; Qatada agrees.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p518/r5.anchor: عن الربيع ، في قوله : لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا يومئذ ، كما ترك المطر الصفا نقيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.claim: The discussion moves from spending in God's path to charity for needy individuals, where reminders and injury are more likely because donor and recipient know one another personally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.anchor: تخلص من غرض التنويه بالإنفاق في سبيل الله إلى التنويه بضرب آخر من الإنفاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r1.claim: The comparison phrase is a settled circumstantial expression describing the addressees: do not act like one who spends for people's eyes and disbelieves in God and the Last Day.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r2.claim: The relative expression denotes a whole class, not a particular person; the comparison vilifies the example and does not make the legal ruling identical, preserving other evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r2.anchor: مراد به جنس وليس مراد به معينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r3.claim: Riyāʾ is an intensive form from seeing, describing frequent display of good deeds; the hamza may be replaced by yāʾ after kasra, producing رياء.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r3.anchor: وهو أن يكثر من إظهار أعماله الحسنة للناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r4.claim: Muslims who seek reward but follow charity with reminders and harm are compared with unbelievers who give only for show and praise, seeking no afterlife reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r4.anchor: والمعنى تشبيه بعض المتصدقين المسلمين الذين يتصدقون طلبا للثواب ويعقبون صدقاتهم بالمن والأذى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r5.claim: Neither group benefits beyond gratifying pride over the weak or the habit of harming them; the image of the rock and washed-away soil extends from unbelieving show-offs to harmful donors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r5.anchor: ووجه الشبه عدم الانتفاع مما أعطوا بأزيد من شفاء ما في صدورهم من حب التطاول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r6.claim: The rock's thin soil looks fit for planting, but a downpour washes it away and leaves smooth bare stone, frustrating the farmer's hope; the image's pronoun can refer to the spender because the parable also depicts the analogue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p48/r6.anchor: فحذفت صفة التراب إيجازا اعتمادا على أن التراب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r1.claim: The more precise image is a rock concealed beneath apparently fertile soil, which the rain strips away; this differs from simply picturing soil on rock being swept off, as in a separate context at 14:18.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r1.anchor: وهذا أحسن وأدق من أن نجعل المعنى تمثيل إنفاق الكافر بحال تراب على صفوان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r2.claim: Alternatively, the comparison particle can describe an implied noun for spending, with a possessive omitted before the relative phrase: spending like the one who spends for show.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r2.anchor: صفة لمصدر محذوف دل عليه ما في لفظ صدقاتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r3.claim: This image reverses the earlier seed yielding seven hundred grains, pairing the two pictures of failed and fruitful spending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r3.anchor: وقد روعي في هذا التمثيل عكس التمثيل لمن ينفق ماله في سبيل الله بحبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r4.claim: The compound comparison maps a promising hope that yields nothing onto the donor's hope for reward, which heedlessness can ruin by prompting reminders and harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49/r4.anchor: ووجه الشبه الأمل في حالة تغر بالنفع ثم لا تلبث ألا تأتي لآملها بما أمله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r1.claim: لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا is deliberately flexible: it may be a state of the spenders, of the figurative rock, an explanatory resumption, a summary, or a state with an omitted relative pronoun.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r2.claim: They cannot retrieve what they gave or benefit from its reward, so nothing remains for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r2.anchor: لا يستطيعون أن يسترجعوه ولا انتفعوا بثوابه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r3.claim: Another possible sense is that they fail to place their earnings where they belong, spending fruitlessly for the afterlife, as the next statement about disbelievers' guidance suggests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى لا يحسنون وضع شيء مما كسبوا موضعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r4.claim: The bare rock yields no crop, as in the description of a person turning his hands over what he spent; God's denial of guidance to disbelievers warns believers against adopting their reminders and harm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p49#2/r4.anchor: مسوق لتحذير المؤمنين من تسرب أحوال الكافرين

SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r1.claim: كالذي may qualify an omitted verbal noun, be circumstantial from the implicit verbal noun on Sibawayh’s analysis, or describe the subject of تبطلوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r1.anchor: فقيل: نعتا لمصدر محذوف أي: لا تبطلوها إبطالا كإبطال الذي ينفق رئاء الناس.

SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r2.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r2.claim: رئاء may qualify an omitted verbal noun, express the purpose of spending, or be a circumstantial description meaning ‘ostentatiously.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r2.anchor: و " رئاء " فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف تقديره: إنفاقا رئاء الناس، كذا ذكره مكي.

SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r3.claim: رئاء is an object-directed verbal noun from راءى, originally رئايا; its reciprocal form suits showing deeds so people praise and magnify the donor.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r3.anchor: والمصدر هنا مضاف للمفعول وهو " الناس " ، ورئاء مصدر راءى كقاتل قتالا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r4.speaker: طلحة
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r4.claim: Ṭalḥa, also reported from ʿĀṣim, reads رياء, changing the first hamza to yāʾ as regular easing after a kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264/r4.anchor: وقرأ طلحة - ويروى عن عاصم -: " رياء " بإبدال الهمزة الأولى ياء،

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r1.claim: The initial ف links the comparison sentence to what precedes it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " لتربط الجملة بما قبلها " وقد تقدم مثله،

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r2.claim: The pronoun in فمثله most likely refers to the ostentatious spender, its nearest antecedent; alternatively it refers to the reproaching donor, comparing him with both images and shifting person and number.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r2.anchor: أظهرهما: أنها تعود على { كالذي ينفق ماله رئآء الناس } لأنه أقرب مذكور.

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r3.claim: صفوان is a large smooth stone; the common form has still fāʾ, while Ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhrī read it with fatḥa, anomalous for a noun pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r3.anchor: والصفوان: حجر كبير أملس، وفيه لغتان: أشهرهما سكون الفاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r4.claim: صفوان may be a plural of صفا, though the plural pattern فعلان is rare.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وجمع " فعل " على " فعلان " قليل ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r5.claim: صفوان is better analyzed as a collective noun, explaining the singular pronoun عليه.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم جنس، قال أبو البقاء: " وهو الأجود، ولذلك عاد الضمير عليه مفردا في قوله: " عليه "

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r6.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī treats صفوان as a singular noun, one of صفي; al-Mubarrad rejects this because صفي is already a plural of صفا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو مفرد، واحد صفي قاله الكسائي، وأنكره المبرد. قال: " لأن صفيا جمع صفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r7.speaker: النحاس
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r7.claim: Al-Naḥḥās allows the kasra form to be singular; al-Kisāʾī also reports it as a plural.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r7.anchor: قال النحاس: " ويجوز أن يكون المسكور الصاد واحدا أيضا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r8.claim: The author rejects al-Kisāʾī’s singular claim: صفوان with kasra is a plural of صفا, comparable to the cited patterns.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r8.anchor: وما قاله الكسائي غير صحيح بل صفوان - يعني بالكسر - جمع لصفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r9.claim: عليه تراب may be a full adjectival clause, or عليه alone may modify صفوان with تراب as subject; the latter is preferred, as with the earlier construction at 2:261.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " عليه " وحده صفة له، و " تراب " فاعل به، وهو أولى

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r10.claim: Arabic also has توراب; ترب الرجل means he became poor, as in 90:16, while أترب means he became rich through privative hamza or by becoming as wealthy as earth.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r10.anchor: ويقال فيه توراب، ويقال: ترب الرجل: افتقر.

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r11.claim: فأصابه coordinates with the verb governing عليه: dust settled on the stone and struck it; the pronoun may refer to stone or dust, while فتركه refers only to the stone.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r11.anchor: " فأصابه " عطف على الفعل الذي تعلق به قوله: " عليه " أي: استقر عليه تراب فأصابه.

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r12.claim: أصاب derives from صاب يصوب, with its alif originating in wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#2/r12.anchor: وألف " أصابه " من واو، لأنه من صاب يصوب.

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r1.claim: وابل means heavy rain; Arabic uses both بلت السماء and أوبل, with موبولة or موبل, and the adjective can stand without an expressed noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r1.anchor: والوابل: المطر الشديد، وبلت السماء تبل، والأرض موبولة، ويقال أيضا: أوبل فهو موبل،

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r2.speaker: النضر بن شميل
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r2.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl lists rain from رش, طش, طل and رذاذ through نضح, هطل and تهتان to heavy وابل and جودة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r2.anchor: قال النضر بن شميل: " أول ما يكون المطر رشا ثم طشا. ثم طلا ورذاذا

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r3.claim: وبيل means harsh or unwholesome; وبيلة is a firewood bundle, and thick objects are called وبيلة by comparison.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r3.anchor: والوبيل: الوخيم، والوبيلة: حزمة الحطب، ومنه قيل للغليظة: وبيلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r4.claim: صلد means bare and smooth, as in a shining bald forehead; it is also an adjective with the stated صلد/يصلد inflection.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r4.anchor: والصلد: الأجرد الأملس، ومنه: " صلد جبين الأصلع ": برق، والصلد أيضا صفة

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r5.speaker: النقاش
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r5.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says صلد is a Hudhayl dialect word.

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r6.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r6.claim: Abān ibn Taghlib defines صلد as soft stone.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r6.anchor: وقال أبان بن تغلب: " الصلد: اللين من الحجارة "

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r7.speaker: علي بن عيسى
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says صلد describes stone, land, and other things with no good in them; قدر صلود is a pot that boils slowly.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#3/r7.anchor: وقال علي ابن عيسى: " هو من الحجارة ما لا خير فيه، وكذلك من الأرضين وغيرها

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r1.claim: لا يقدرون may be independent or circumstantial from الذي; plural agreement follows its generic meaning after singular-form reference, as in 2:17.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r1.anchor: لأن المراد بالذي الجنس، فلذلك جاز الحمل على لفظه مرة في قوله: " ماله " و " لا يؤمن " " فمثله "

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya claims Arabic normally uses literal form first and meaning second, while reversing that order is ugly; the author has already challenged the rule.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r2.anchor: وقد زعم ابن عطية أن مهيع كلام العرب الحمل على اللفظ أولا ثم المعنى ثانيا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r3.claim: The plural pronoun may instead address the believers from the prior command, a distant shift, or refer to donors who cannot benefit from their charity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r3.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في " يقدرون " عائد على المخاطبين بقوله: { يأيها الذين آمنوا لا تبطلوا }

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ objects that لا يقدرون cannot be circumstantial from الذي because فمثله intervenes; the author says the interruption reinforces the point like a parenthesis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r4.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ولا يجوز أن يكون " ولا يقدرون " حالا من " الذي

SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:264#4/r5.claim: The charity is called a gain or acquisition in this passage.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r7.claim: The theological principle is that sins do not erase good deeds; the issue is that God does not accept a particular gift whose donor will reproach or harm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r7.anchor: العقيدة أن السيئات لا تبطل الحسنات، فقال جمهور العلماء في هذه الآية: إن الصدقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r8.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r8.claim: The majority say a gift from someone whom God knows will reproach or harm is not accepted as charity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r8.anchor: إن الصدقة التي يعلم الله في صاحبها أنه يمن أو يؤذي فإنها لا تتقبل صدقة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r9.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r9.claim: Another view says God gives the angel a sign so the gift is not written down.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r9.anchor: وقيل بل جعل الله للملك عليها أمارة فلا يكتبها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya favors the latter account: reproach reveals an insincere intention, so the act was never true charity; this does not invalidate another gift whose sound intention it does not expose.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r10.anchor: وهذا حسن، لأن ما نتلقى نحن عن المعقول من بني آدم فهو أن المن المؤذي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r11.claim: The donor who reproaches is compared with one who gives to show off rather than for God; ostentation derives from seeing and amounts to display and mutual boasting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r11.anchor: ثم مثل الله هذا الذي يمن ويؤذي بحسب مقدمة نيته بالذي ينفق رئاء لا لوجه الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r12.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r12.claim: Al-Mahdawī supplies “the invalidation of” as an implied word in the comparison’s syntax.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r12.anchor: قال المهدوي والتقدير كإبطال الذي ينفق رئاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r13.claim: The ostentatious donor may be an open unbeliever seeking praise, or a hypocrite who outwardly professes faith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r13.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر يحتمل أن يريد الكافر الظاهر الكفر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r14.claim: A smooth rock covered by soil appears fertile until heavy rain strips it bare; at resurrection the show-off’s empty gift is similarly exposed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p357/r14.anchor: فإذا أصاب الصفوان وابل من المطر انكشف ذلك التراب وبقي صلدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r1.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r1.claim: Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif reads riyāʾ without hamza; the reading is also transmitted from ʿĀṣim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r1.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن مصرف «رياء الناس» بغير همز. ورويت عن عاصم.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r2.claim: Ṣafwān is a large, smooth rock; grammarians differ whether it is a plural or a singular with variant forms, and al-Mubarrad rejects those analyses in favor of a plural of ṣafā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r2.anchor: والصفوان الحجر الكبير الأملس. قيل هو جمع واحدته صفواته.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r3.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r3.claim: A line by Imruʾ al-Qays compares something slipping from a horse’s back to a smooth stone surface.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r3.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: [الطويل] كميت يزل اللبد عن حال متنه ... كما زلت الصفواء بالمتنزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r4.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r4.claim: Abū Dhuʾayb compares repeated blows to a stone at al-Mushaqqar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r4.anchor: وقال أبو ذؤيب: [الكامل] حتى كأني للحوادث مروة ... بصفا المشقر كل يوم تقرع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r5.speaker: الزهري وابن المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r5.claim: They read ṣafwān with fatḥa on the fāʾ, a dialectal form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r5.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وابن المسيب «صفوان» بفتح الفاء، وهي لغة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r6.claim: Wābil is strong, abundant rain that runs over the land; ṣald is bare, hard, smooth stone and can also describe a bald head.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r6.anchor: والوابل الكثير القوي من المطر وهو الذي يسيل على وجه الأرض، والصلد من الحجارة الأملس الصلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r7.speaker: رؤبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r7.claim: Ruʾba’s verse uses ṣilād for a smooth, shining forehead without hair.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r7.anchor: ومنه قول رؤبة: [الرجز] براق أصلاد الجبين الأجله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r8.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r8.claim: Al-Naqqāsh says ṣald means hairless or smooth in the Hudhayl dialect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r8.anchor: قال النقاش: الصلد الأجرد بلغة هذيل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r9.claim: “They cannot” refers to ostentatious donors, unable to benefit from the reward of their spending; the wording shifts from the singular relative “one who” to plural by normal Arabic usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r9.anchor: لا يقدرون على الانتفاع بثواب شيء من إنفاقهم ذلك وهو كسبهم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r10.claim: “God does not guide the unbelieving people” may mean those who die in unbelief, that He has not guided them in their unbelief, or that their spending is unguided while they remain unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r10.anchor: إما عموم يراد به الخصوص في الموافي على الكفر، وإما أن يراد به أنه لم يهدهم في كفرهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r11.claim: The language and interpretation given for this verse are drawn from the exegetes, although their wording was not always summarized specifically under the nullification of charity by reproach.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p358/r11.anchor: وما ذكرته في هذه الآية من تفسير لغة وتقويم معنى فإنه مسند عن المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r1.claim: Do not nullify charity means do not nullify its reward, as in the case of a hypocritical show-off who does not believe in God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r1.anchor: لا تبطلوا ثوابها كما تبطل ثواب صدقة المرائي الذي لا يؤمن بالله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r2.claim: Safwan is smooth stone, wabil is heavy rain, and sald means smooth; al-Zajjaj also calls it smooth stone, while Tha'lab glosses sald as bare or clean.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة الصفوان الحجر والوابل أشد المطر والصلد الأملس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r3.claim: “It left it bare” means the stone had nothing on it afterward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس وقتادة ﴿ فتركه صلدا ﴾ قالا ليس عليه شيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r4.claim: The stone-and-rain image represents a show-off whose charity yields no reward on Judgment Day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p318#3/r4.anchor: وهذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى للمرائي بنفقته لا يقدر يوم القيامة على ثواب شيء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r3.claim: The verse declares that flaunting a gift or harming its recipient nullifies charity, so its reward cannot outweigh the sin of those acts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r3.anchor: فأخبر أن الصدقة تبطل بما يتبعها من المن والأذى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r4.claim: A show-off gives to win public praise or a reputation for generosity while neglecting God's approval and reward; his deeds vanish like rain washing soil off smooth rock, even if people see apparent good works.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r4.anchor: فأظهر لهم أنه يريد وجه الله وإنما قصده مدح الناس له أو شهرته بالصفات الجميلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk explains the hypocritical spender's likeness as also covering someone who follows a gift with boasting or harm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p694/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك: والذي يتبع نفقته منا أو أذى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r5.claim: The warning compares nullifying charity by reminders and harm to a hypocrite's giving for public display without seeking God's pleasure or afterlife reward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r5.anchor: أي لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والأذى كإبطال المنافق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib read صفوان on the pattern of كروان.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340/r6.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن المسيب ( صفوان ) بوزن كروان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r1.claim: A wabil is rain with large drops.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r2.claim: Ṣald means stripped bare of its soil, as in describing the shining bald forehead.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r2.anchor: أجرد نقيا من التراب الذي كان عليه ومنه صلد جبين الأصلع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r3.claim: Their earned deeds yield nothing, like dust scattered away.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r4.claim: The comparison can be circumstantial: do not invalidate charity while resembling the person who spends in ostentation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r4.anchor: ان تكون الكاف في محل النصب على الحال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r5.claim: The plural ‘they cannot’ refers to the class or group of spenders; al-ladhī and man alternate in meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p340#2/r5.anchor: أراد بالذي ينفق الجنس أو الفريق الذي ينفق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r11.claim: Reminding and harming nullifies charity's merit without nullifying its reward, or instead nullifies its effect in the recipient's heart.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r11.anchor: يريد إبطال الفضل دون الثواب . ويحتمل وجها ثانيا : إبطال موقعها في نفس المعطى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r12.claim: An ostentatious spender who lacks faith receives no reward because he did not intend God; unlike him, the sincere giver's reward remains though reminders erase the gift's merit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r12.anchor: القاصد بنفقته الرياء غير مثاب , لأنه لم يقصد وجه الله , فيستحق ثوابه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r13.speaker: أبان بن تغلب
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r13.claim: Safwan may mean a smooth stone named for its clarity or a stone softer than other stones, as A-ban ibn Taghlib relates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r13.anchor: أنه ألين من الحجارة , حكاه أبان بن تغلب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r14.claim: Wabil is heavy rain with large drops and forceful impact; sald is hard stone or barren earth, like a stone that grows nothing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r15.claim: What they earned means what they spent, since they sought to earn reward through it; the image shows ostentation erasing reward and reproach erasing merit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p337/r15.anchor: لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا } يعني مما أنفقوا , فعبر عن النفقة بالكسب , لأنهم قصدوا بها الكسب

MUQATIL:2:264/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:264/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:264/r1.claim: Reproach makes a donor's charity void because it injures the recipient; the verse compares this with a showy spender who disbelieves in God and resurrection.
MUQATIL:2:264/r1.anchor: يقول: يمن بها فإن ذلك أذى لصاحبها وكل صدقة يمن بها صاحبها على المعطى، فإن المن يبطلها،

MUQATIL:2:264/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:264/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:264/r2.claim: A disbelieving show-off's spending and a believer's charity followed by reproach both yield no reward, like a stone slab whose soil a heavy rain washes away.
MUQATIL:2:264/r2.anchor: فى مثله: { فمثله كمثل صفوان } ، يعنى الصفا، { عليه تراب فأصابه وابل } ،

MUQATIL:2:264/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:264/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:264/r3.claim: They will have no reward for what they spent on the Day of Resurrection; the same image appears in the comparison of disbelievers' deeds to windblown ashes.
MUQATIL:2:264/r3.anchor: وذلك قوله سبحانه: { لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا } ، يقول: لا يقدرون على ثواب شىء مما أنفقوا يوم القيامة وذلك قوله عز وجل:

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r1.claim: The kāf grammatically describes an omitted verbal noun: do not nullify charity with invalidation like that of the hypocrite who gives for display and lacks faith in God and the Last Day.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r1.anchor: الكاف نصب صفة مصدر محذوف والتقدير بطلا مثل ابطال الذى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r2.claim: The smooth rock covered with dust represents a hypocrite's useless spending; a downpour strips it bare, leaving no reward for what was earned.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r2.anchor: مثله ونفقته التى لا ينتفع بها ألبته بحجر أملس عليه تراب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r3.claim: The singular relative can denote a class or group, explaining why the text shifts to plural 'they cannot'; alternatively the kāf is circumstantial.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r3.anchor: أراد بالذى ينفق الجنس أو الفريق الذى ينفق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p129#3/r4.claim: God does not guide people who choose disbelief for as long as they remain committed to it.

ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r1.claim: Al-mann is reminding a recipient of one’s gift and claiming credit; al-adhā is reproaching the recipient.
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r1.anchor: فالمن أن تمن بما أعطيت وتعتد به

ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r2.claim: Such conduct nullifies charity like a hypocrite’s gift, made to appear faithful rather than to seek God’s reward; the smooth stone’s soil is washed away by a heavy downpour.
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r2.anchor: فأعلم الله عز وجل أن المن والأذى يبطلان الصدقة

ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347/r3.claim: Ṣafwān is a smooth rock; wabil is heavy rain, which removes all soil from the rock, just as hypocritical or hurtful giving is nullified.

ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p347#2/r1.claim: God does not guide disbelievers by reason of their disbelief; another reported explanation is that He does not make guidance their recompense.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r1.claim: 'Invalidating' means that the particular charity followed by reminders or harm is not accepted and loses reward; it does not invalidate unrelated good deeds, since sins do not annul good deeds as a general rule.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r1.anchor: الصدقة التي يمن بها ويؤذي، لا غيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r2.claim: Most scholars say God does not accept a donation when He knows its donor will later reproach or harm the recipient; another view says God gives the recording angel a sign not to record it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r2.anchor: قال جمهور العلماء في هذه الآية: إن الصدقة التي يعلم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r3.claim: Arabic idiom calls a gift used for reproach a 'black hand,' an unasked gift a 'white hand,' and a gift prompted by a request a 'green hand.'
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r3.anchor: ولما يعطي عن غير مسألة: يد بيضاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r4.speaker: بعض البلغاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r4.claim: A rhetorician says that reminding someone of a favor forfeits gratitude, while admiring one's own deed destroys its reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r4.anchor: وقال بعض البلغاء: من من بمعروفه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r5.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r5.claim: When Ibn Sirin heard a man enumerate favors to another, he told him to stop: beneficence has no good in it once it is counted aloud.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r5.anchor: وسمع ابن سيرين رجلا يقول لرجل:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r6.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r6.claim: A Prophetic report warns that reminding others of a favor erases gratitude and reward, then recites this verse; no grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r6.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r7.claim: Malik disliked paying obligatory alms to relatives for fear of seeking their praise, reminding them, or receiving repayment that compromises sincerity; he preferred strangers and having another distribute it when the ruler is unjust.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r7.anchor: كره مالك لهذه الآية أن يعطي الرجل صدقته الواجبة أقاربه لئلا يعتاض منهم الحمد والثناء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r8.claim: If voluntary secret charity loses its reward, it simply becomes as though never done; if obligatory alms loses reward, the giver faces a threat as though he failed to perform it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r8.anchor: وهذا بخلاف صدقة التطوع السر لأن ثوابها إذا حبط سلم من الوعيد وصار في حكم من لم يفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r9.claim: Grammatically, the comparison's kāf can be accusative as an adjective for an omitted verbal noun or can function circumstantially.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r9.anchor: الكاف في موضع نصب، أي إبطال «كالذي»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r10.claim: The harmful donor is compared to a show-off who gives for reputation, like a disbeliever seeking praise; rain strips dust from a smooth rock and exposes its barren surface, just as these motives expose the intention and erase the gift.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264/r10.anchor: مثل الله تعالى الذي يمن ويؤذي بصدقته بالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس لا لوجه الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.claim: One interpretation is that reminder and harm erase the gift's excellence, not its reward: a show-off earns nothing like a disbeliever, while a sincere donor originally merits reward but loses the gift's excellence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالآية إبطال الفضل دون الثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r2.claim: Another view says only the reward after the donor begins reminding and harming is lost; earlier reward remains, but further multiplication stops, as charity otherwise grows like a mountain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r2.anchor: وقد قيل: إنما يبطل من ثواب صدقته من وقت منه وإيذائه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r3.claim: The author prefers the first interpretation of the preceding disagreement as the more apparent one.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r4.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says ṣafwān is a collective with singular ṣafwāna; another reported view treats ṣafwān as singular, like 'stone.'

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r5.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r5.claim: Al-Kisa'i calls ṣafwān singular and gives ṣafwān, ṣafī, and ṣafiyy as plurals; al-Mubarrad rejects ṣafī as the plural of ṣafā, like qafā/qafī.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r5.anchor: وقال الكسائي: صفوان واحد وجمعه صفوان وصفي وصفي، وأنكره المبرد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and al-Zuhri read ṣafwān with a fatḥa on the fāʾ, a dialectal form; Qutrub also records the form.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن المسيب والزهري «صفوان» بتحريك الفاء، وهي لغة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:264#2/r7.speaker: النحاس
